operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Headline plus inset motion module". Objective: Turn many motion assets into a consistent vertical ad family. Visual rule: Keep the wrapper fixed while swapping the inner motion, hook and offer. Beats, in order: - 0–1.5 s: Large headline occupies the upper region; media window is already present. Shows Brand color, Module A, Headline. - 1.5–4.5 s: Inset media demonstrates the premise. Shows Brand color, Module A, Module A line. - 4.5–6.5 s: A result or continuation plays inside the same window. Shows Brand color, Module B, Module B line. - 6.5–8 s: Result freezes or settles while the headline gains a short payoff. Shows Brand color, Module B, Payoff. - 8–10 s: CTA strip is visible below the media frame. Shows Brand color, Module B, Logo, Call to action. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: hook (Headline: hook, at most 7 words); benefitA (Module A line: module a, at most 7 words); benefitB (Module B line: module b, at most 7 words); payoff (Payoff: payoff, at most 7 words); cta (Call to action: cta, at most 4 words) - images: moduleA (Module A: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Large headline occupies the upper region; media window is already present. | Inset media demonstrates the premise.); moduleB (Module B: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: A result or continuation plays inside the same window. | Result freezes or settles while the headline gains a short payoff. | CTA strip is visible below the media frame.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: CTA strip is visible below the media frame.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
